statement: MasterSite catalogs Commodities — Kalshi Research Exchange in Markets & Trading Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Evidence-first paper-trading lab for Kalshi event contracts, organised around an automated forward-test desk. 23 return-seeking strategy personas (plus 4 gated ones) trade open Kalshi contracts on paper twice an hour from a scheduled, read-only GitHub Actions collector, and every fill, exit, settlement, intent, mark and order book is committed back to the repository. Two backtests run on verified official Kalshi price data: the original hand-collected sample (3 settled markets, 130 verified bars, 5 personas), deliberately frozen, and an archive backtest replayed bar by bar over the candle archive the collector now stores (45 markets, 1,691 verified bars, 199 trades, 9 rule sets, with per-trade equity curves and a walk-forward stability split). An execution-realism check re-reads every simulated fill against Kalshi's own published trade tape via GET /markets/trades and reports the difference in cents, with a committed live result of 158 fills compared at a median absolute desk-minus-tape gap of 1.00 cent. A season health audit (scripts/audit_season.py) checks the schedule, ledger coverage, storage compaction, signal adapters and the tape summary, re-reads settled markets against the official API on the runner, and refuses to let verify_data.py pass if anything disagrees. Simulation only: nothing submits orders to Kalshi and no API key exists anywhere in the project.
flags: Newly added this pass: HeatConfirm, a weather rule discovered in a third-party Reddit backtest post, is traded forward precisely because its backtest claim is someone else's — the repository labels the source discovery-only and never a price source, and testing the claim forward IS the experiment.

The desk quantifies its own cron reliability rather than assuming it: IRR-34 (2026-09-21) records scripts/audit_season.py counting every scheduled :07/:37 UTC slot against committed cycles, and the committed audit shows 4 cycles with API errors out of 361 evidence-bound ledger events.
Persona count moved 20 -> 23 and the source registry 63 -> 70 entries between the 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 audits; treat all counts here as point-in-time.

A season-rollover layer landed during this audit ('Extend evidence-first desk across archive and season rollover'), adding data/seasons.json, a per-strategy JSON page set, an audit history log and browser plus smoke tests for the rollover path. It changed none of the published figures above.

statement: MasterSite catalogs GEMSDOE — Geologic Mapping Prize Challenge in Science & ML Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Evidence-backed site for the DOE GEMS Prize Challenge on DrivenData ($300,000 total prize — $50k initial, $250k final — ending 2026-12-03): predicting geothermal faults in the GeoDAWN region under a distance-weighted Tversky metric, with a 19-band feature stack. Session-19 status read from STATUS.md: all four block-holdout folds are now committed and the memorisation-vs-transfer gap is reported as a spread rather than a point — fold 0 +0.0114, fold 1 −0.0070, fold 2 +0.0139, fold 3 +0.0093, mean +0.006904, spread 0.020935, positive in 3 of 4 — and because no fold reaches the ≥12 resampling units a readable block-bootstrap interval needs, the scorer itself flags every per-fold interval `interval_readable: false`, so the honest reading is 'no clear memorisation, no clear transfer gain' with the full-grid 0.099859 (reproduced digit-for-digit on a runner) retained as the selection statistic. The pseudo-label contrast is measured on every committed truth population and points in opposite directions on the two components, but it has now FIRED TWICE and STATUS.md is explicit that 'quoting either one alone would overstate the precision'. The first fire gave held-out blocks 0.0806 → 0.1841 (+0.1036, P=0.999) on the new-fault-like proxy against 0.2113 → 0.1239 (−0.0874, P=0.001) on catalogue labels, deriving TRADE_OFF_PROXY_GAINS_CATALOGUE_LOSSES; the second fire — same seed, same config, same partition, different runner — measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue −0.1079, deriving GAIN_ON_THE_COMBINED_SURROGATE. value.description: A deliberately small, evidence-first betting-research workbench whose central finding is that none of its strategies beat the market on the pilot sample. Football pilot: a 27-match Bundesliga 1 2024/25 sample (matchdays 1, 10 and 20, fixtures committed and sha256-verified) reached 27/27 dual-source result agreement between OpenLigaDB and football-data.co.uk on an exact-minute UK-time join, yielding 613 odds snapshots (405 on 1X2 plus 208 on a newly added over/under 2.5 goals market) across 9 strategies — all nine negative on both markets, with confidence intervals including zero and a Holm-adjusted p of 1.0. Sport two is ice hockey (DEL 2024/25) on the same open-licensed OpenLigaDB path, with overtime- and shootout-aware final-score selection and one Elo strategy that produces predictions only: 11 graded predictions, 7 correct (63.6%), Brier 0.4737, and PnL reported as unavailable rather than zero because no permissioned odds path exists for hockey. Sport three is darts (PDC), prediction-only, where the cold 2025 pool made 0 selections in 141 opportunities because the maximum probability of 0.551 never cleared the 0.60 threshold — recorded as silence with no refit — while the full 2025-26 pool graded 39 of 48 correct (81.25%) at Brier 0.349. Identity is labelled per sport: football verified, hockey and darts probable on a single source. 258 offline pytest tests cover fixtures, odds parsing, time-zone handling, settlement, walk-forward invariants and each pilot's guarantees, and every number carries a licence and a retrieval date with the ODbL attribution for OpenLigaDB stated on the site itself.

statement: MasterSite catalogs ShoulderPain — Research-Backed Shoulder & Scapula Pain Guide in Health & Personal Guides; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Source-linked GitHub Pages guide to shoulder and shoulder-blade ('wing') pain, written around one stated context — a male adult aged about 36-40, left-side sleeping, a possible workout injury, prolonged computer use and limited room space — and explicitly educational information rather than a diagnosis or a personalised rehabilitation plan, with emergency and urgent warning signs given priority over exercises, furniture or symptom logging. Ten pages share one static template and compact navigation: start, medical advice, treatment, exercises, desk and room, furniture and prices, care costs, an optional log, sources and audit, and next steps; all research content works without JavaScript and no sign-in or symptom entry is required. The current revision is a deliberate narrowing rather than an expansion. It reviewed the pre-existing site at commit e1c63c4 and, in its own words, 'replaces blanket verification/completeness claims with a narrower, auditable source register, simplifies the UI and corrects unsafe or unverified assumptions', keeping the previous site in Git history. Twenty official pages were opened directly on 2026-09-20 — MedlinePlus, NHS, AAOS/ASES, CSP, OSHA, CMS, five furniture manufacturers or sellers, and Luna — and data/sources.json records each source's section, a short excerpt, its scope and its check date, with government and medical-society guidance kept separate from commercial product information. data/claims.json maps source-bearing content units to references and source-file lines: 90 review units, described as a review aid and 'not an automated truth certificate'. Exercises were reduced to four source-checked examples carrying exact AAOS HTML doses and supervision boundaries. Five furniture listings give exact variant and price boundaries with folding trade-offs, and no product is claimed to fit an unmeasured room or to treat shoulder pain; the one care price quoted is an official provider example ($135 self-pay per visit at Luna), not a nationwide average, and other unverified medical costs are explicitly left unpriced. REVIEW.md documents three passes and eight source irregularities found while reading, including a COMHOMA price where $54.49 was the selected White variant and $25.50 the discount, a VIVO desk that folds against the wall but is not quickly detached, a Lillipad whose specifications claim a 700 lb static test while its FAQ says 350 lb and neither replaces the 75 lb operational rating, and a Luna search excerpt showing $125 where both directly opened pages showed $135. The optional log is local-only, retains the `shoulderpain-log-v1` key so prior entries can still be read or imported if valid, and validates numbers, booleans, calendar dates and shape; invalid entries are counted and never rounded or silently converted, invalid persisted data blocks edits rather than being overwritten, raw JSON export is available for recovery, cross-tab changes block saves until reload, spreadsheet formula injection is mitigated on CSV export, and the bounded import size was raised to 20 MB so the 5,000-entry schema can import its own backups. Its former clinical 'improving/worsening' classifier and calendar-based advice were removed on the grounds that sparse logs should not reassure someone or postpone assessment, and the summary is now descriptive only. Validation reports 8 Node unit tests and 31 Chromium browser tests passing, automated axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 AA checks passing on all ten pages at 390px and 1440px, and no page-level horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768 or 1440px. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20.
flags: Its own verification policy refuses the strongest claims a directory reader might assume: 'Unknown or conflicting facts stay visibly unresolved. No claim of independent clinical verification or zero errors', and 'Automated checks cannot establish medical accuracy'. REVIEW.md adds that no clinician independently reviewed the personalised suitability of the information, and that link integrity, automated accessibility and browser tests are not medical validation.

Deliberately narrower than the version it replaced. The prior revision carried a 56-source register (S1-S56), four logged review passes, 32 logged corrections and a 32-row irregularity table; this one carries 20 opened sources, three passes, 8 source irregularities and a 6-row next-steps table. Its stated reason is worth quoting because it is the opposite of the usual instinct: 'The guide is a focused, source-linked starting set, not all possible diseases or products. Further expansion should improve evidence rather than inflate a count' (IRR-57).

Now has a build and test step, unlike the version previously described here: npm ci, npm run build (claim ledger plus ten static root HTML pages), npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser (Playwright) and npm run serve, with the shared page layout in tools/build.py and Python 3 and Node 22 used in validation. Visitors need neither. Committed root HTML means the Pages configuration needs no runtime build.

Browser tests were run against an npm-distributed Chromium 153 binary extracted outside Git because the standard Playwright browser download and Debian package retrieval were blocked by sandbox networking; REVIEW.md states plainly that 'this is not an unexecuted test claim', and CI uses the normal Playwright installation on GitHub-hosted runners. statement: MasterSite catalogs WoW Forever Hub — Source-Verified World of Warcraft Guide in Gaming & Guides; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Source-verified information site for World of Warcraft: Forever (the repository dates Blizzard's launch to 4 November 2026 with raids unlocking 9 December 2026), published as fourteen static pages — index, roadmap, pvp, classes, class-pvp, gear, gold, addons, beta, sources, method, data-api, site-patterns and work-plan. Every published statement is carried in a claims ledger (data/claims.js; the repository counts 183 claims today, IDs deliberately not contiguous) with an evidence class of official, press, datamine, guide, ours, unknown or community, backed by a source registry in data/sources.js, and checked in CI by tools/check-ledger.mjs and tools/check-sources.mjs. Class tier lists, Best-in-Slot item lists and gold-per-hour figures are deliberately omitted because the beta is capped at level 20 (30 later) and items are hidden until they drop.
flags: The repository records its own irregularity log I-1 through I-24 on method.html, and states plainly what it refuses to publish rather than filling gaps with estimates.

Grew from nine to fourteen pages between the 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-20 audits (class-pvp, addons, beta, data-api and site-patterns added) and its ledger grew from C001-C110 to 183 claims, so its totals remain a point-in-time read printed on its home page from the data files.
value.title: WoW Forever Hub — Source-Verified World of Warcraft Guide
value.verifiedBasis: Re-stamped at commit f7c83bc after 1 commit, verified benign rather than assumed so. The compare 329826c...f7c83bc touches exactly two files — tools/feed-state.json (+23/-37) and tools/source-state.json (+627/-499) — in a commit titled 'chore(source-watch): update source fingerprints and feed observations'. These are the source-watch tool's own observation state, not site content: no page, no claim and no ledger row changed. The description's two countable assertions were nevertheless re-counted against this commit rather than carried on faith: the repository publishes 14 static pages plus 404.html (ls *.html returns 15 files, of which 404.html is the Pages fallback), and data/claims.js holds 183 claim entries counted by matching the id field, matching the description's 'counts 183 claims today, IDs deliberately not contiguous' — the file's own header comment instructs readers to report the claim count and never the highest ID. Reproduce: git clone https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/WoWForever.git && grep -cE "id: *.C[0-9]+" data/claims.js.

Two backtests run on verified official Kalshi price data: the original hand-collected sample (3 settled markets, 130 verified bars, 5 personas), deliberately frozen, and an archive backtest replayed bar by bar over the candle archive the collector now stores (45 markets, 1,691 verified bars, 199 trades, 9 rule sets, with per-trade equity curves and a walk-forward stability split). Simulation only: nothing submits orders to Kalshi and no API key exists anywhere in the project.

statement: MasterSite catalogs FLABSENGY — FantasyLabs Projection Reverse Engineering in Sports Data & Scoreboards; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Clean-room study of the FantasyLabs DFS projection system plus an original Python engine that rebuilds the metrics the vendor documents publicly — no subscription data, no scraped pages, no proprietary weights, and an explicit record of what was refused. Evidence counted at commit f927bab: docs/ledger.html holds 49 source rows inside an S1-S50 range, research/IRREGULARITIES.md carries 16 flagged items I1-I16, research/REQUIREMENTS.md maps acceptance requirements R1-R17, and engine/fantasylab_engine/metrics.py defines 14 functions covering Plus/Minus, implied points from a salary-expectation fit, Pts/Sal, consistency, upside, duds, bargain rating, opponent Plus/Minus, salary change and percentile rank. `pytest -q` was executed in this audit and returned 79 passed. Where the vendor's own official glossaries disagree — the NFL defines Duds as fewer than half a salary-based expectation while the NBA and MLB glossaries define it as at least half a standard deviation below it — the engine implements both variants and documents which one is the default; where a methodology is not public at all (ownership projection, Pro Trend definitions, salary-regression parameters) it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
flags: Two of the README's headline counts are off against the files they describe. Its table says '50 sources' where docs/ledger.html holds 49 rows — the ledger states in terms that 'Missing ID S15 is reserved (not used)' — and 'All 19 publicly documented metrics' where docs/metrics.html carries 20 metric rows. This entry publishes the counted values 49 and 20; the disagreement is IRR-74.

The refusals are the substance of the audit, not an omission from it: I1-I3 record that the request to rebuild whatever sits behind the paywall would be paywall circumvention and reproduction of copyrighted subscription content, and that the Terms governing fantasylabs.com ban scraping, robots and reverse engineering of source code. The repository therefore limited itself to a handful of direct public page reads and wrote the engine from published metric definitions.

Two live findings about the vendor are reported and deliberately not exploited: fantasylabs.com/articles-new/ is publicly reachable and labelled '(Test)' in a search index (I10), and a search index surfaced a raw JSON player-news API path that appeared to need no authentication (I11). The endpoint was not interrogated further and is not consumed.

FanDuel scoring is taken from the operator's own rules page against secondary DFS guides that claim FanDuel has no yardage bonuses (I12); the engine trusts official pages only and excludes the secondary tables from its config.

statement: MasterSite catalogs FUTURESCOMMODITIES — Commodity Futures Paper-Trading Competition in Markets & Trading Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Commodity research, strategy and paper-trading competition platform in which every published price carries the URL and SHA-256 of the exact HTTP response it came from, plus the provenance log of the run that produced it. At commit 16e981f the catalog in engine/strategies/index.mjs holds 17 strategies, one per username, trading three kinds of instrument: Kalshi commodity/prediction event contracts, Kalshi perpetual futures where the exchange publishes them, and exchange-listed commodity futures on MOEX FORTS. config/competition.json sets the season to 2026-09-22 through 2027-09-22 with 100,000 USD starting cash. The last committed tick predates that expansion, so the competition state it published still covers 12 strategies: data/verification/report.json records 44 trades checked, 34 fully verified and 10 anomalies, 6 intents that could not execute, and 74 instruments (45 Kalshi, 4 Kalshi margin, 25 MOEX FORTS), with fills split 26 quote-based, 18 taken from published ladders and 0 modelled maker fills. data/reports/summary.json shows 40 entries and 4 exits, 6 of the 12 booked strategies holding open positions, and equity spread from 100,000.00 down to 99,890.42 (-0.11 percent). A separate research file, data/reports/backtests.json, re-runs 6 documented rules over committed official daily histories for 817 simulated daily-close trades and marks 4 strategies unavailable for backtesting. Data comes only from keyless official endpoints — Kalshi Trade API v2, MOEX ISS, EIA and USDA AMS Market News — and the engine uses nothing but the Node standard library. Every fill is simulated: no order is ever sent to an exchange.
flags: Catalog and competition state disagree because the repository moved while it was being read. Commit a64a347 ('Expand to 17 strategies, re-enable cross-venue basis on verified contract data, add research backtests and live-desk/research site sections', 2026-09-22T23:04:47Z) added five strategies and re-enabled @basis-hunter, but the tick it sits on top of was generated at 23:03:54Z and still reports coverage.strategies == 12 with a 12-row leaderboard. Both numbers are published here with the file each came from instead of being reconciled. IRR-75.

All 10 verification anomalies are the same check, instrument_present_in_published_universe — instruments that settled and dropped out of the universe file. They are reported on the site and never silently corrected.

Of the 6 documented backtest rules only two recorded any trades at all (Metals Settlement Trend 674 and Channel Breakout 20/10 on MOEX metals 143); the other four recorded 0. The 817 total is the sum of total_trades_recorded across the six, and the file's own caveat states that a backtest 'is never a track record and never a season trade'. Its fills are at published daily prices with no depth, no slippage, no participation cap and no queue position.

Where an exchange blocks scripted access — CME Group, ICE, LME, Eurex, JPX, SGX, B3 — contract specifications are cited from official pages but no price is simulated, and the strategy is labelled unavailable for backtesting rather than filled from a proxy.

This is a returns-only simulator by design: strategies are deliberately not risk-managed because the competition is scored on returns alone, and the only hard constraints are real liquidity from the published order books and a one-position-per-instrument rule.

value.description: Autonomous, evidence-first research engine that runs on a timer with no manual input: .github/workflows/think.yml fires on a */30 * * * * cron, reads official public data, appends to a claims ledger, regenerates the site and documentation and commits its own output, so a cycle that reads nothing still publishes and says so. A cycle is seven stages, each a separate module that can fail without stopping the others — a failed stage becomes an entry in the irregularity register and the cycle still publishes. Figures below are the repository's own regenerated counts block at commit eda549e, cycle 24, generated 2026-09-22T23:43:29Z: 20,947 accepted claims in the ledger (5,840 under the schema-v2 strict trace contract and 15,107 under the legacy contract reported but not upgraded; 13,842 captured from accepted source reads, 7,085 derived by recorded arithmetic and 20 negative proofs of absence), 0 claims rejected by the evidence gate, 2,122 derived claims rechecked this cycle with 0 that no longer recompute, 157 topics in the library (6 new), 408 published insights, 1,056 forecasts issued and 717 scored against outcomes with 2,891 still waiting for an observation and 0 that can never be scored, 28 ideas in the competition with 1 promoted, 27 open irregularities (2 new), 31 registered sources of which 28 are verified by a recorded live read and 3 are currently blocked, 62 reads ok against 4 failed this cycle out of 66 planned with 0 refused by the cap, 2,226,743 bytes read, and 0 manual inputs required. IRREGULARITIES.md at the same timestamp records 122 irregularities registered in total — 6 critical, 71 warn and 45 info — of which 27 are open, 95 resolved and 21 standing, where standing means a structural limit that deliberately does not auto-resolve. The 350-test suite was executed in this audit and passed.
flags: This entry was published as 'MasterSelfLearn — Empty Placeholder Repository' from the 2026-09-21 audit, when the repository was one commit holding a single 15-byte README created twenty seconds after SelfLearn's (IRR-71). It is now a 42-commit, 111-file engine with a seven-stage pipeline, a claims ledger, three GitHub workflows and a 350-test suite. The placeholder description had become flatly false and is rewritten here from the repository's own files. IRR-84.

Every number in this description has a shelf life of at most 30 minutes, by design: the counts block is regenerated by msl/pipeline.py on every cron cycle and the README states that 'Quoting any figure outside this block means quoting something the next cycle has already superseded'. The repository moved from fe488ed to eda549e (cycle 24) while this pass was reading it. Treat all figures as cycle-24 values at 2026-09-22T23:43:29Z, not as current ones.

The ledger's own honesty split is published rather than collapsed into one total: of 20,947 accepted claims only 5,840 satisfy the schema-v2 strict trace contract, while 15,107 remain under the legacy trace contract and are reported but not upgraded. A reader who quotes 20,947 as strictly-traced claims would be overstating the evidence by roughly a factor of 3.6.

Forecast scoring is bounded and says so: 717 of 1,056 forecasts issued this cycle have been scored against outcomes, 2,891 are waiting for an observation, and 0 are recorded as can never be scored. Sources are similarly graded — 28 of 31 verified by a recorded live read, 3 currently blocked, 0 never probed — and 21 standing irregularities are structural limits the owner is meant to keep seeing rather than transient failures that auto-resolve.
The root of the repository is the published site (index.html plus 12 further HTML pages, app.js and styles.css) and Pages publishes from main /, so this entry classifies as app.

value.description: This site: the master directory and line-by-line verification ledger for every GitHub Pages site published under buffedlizard55-lab, plus a verified check of kanlerxz87-cyber. Each of the 63 entries carries a sourced description, creation date, last-updated date, commit telemetry, Pages build source, the commit its prose was read at, and official API links for independent manual review. Two views — a card grid and a table — are retuned by a per-browser Density preference: the table is compact by default because its job is comparison, dropping rows from about 60px to about 29px with a fixed-width name column and the curated title clipped to one line, and below 900px the same nine cells re-stack into labelled lines so a phone reads a card per site instead of scrolling a ~1,000px table sideways. value.description: Auditable MLB research and paper-betting platform running the loop research -> discover -> verify -> model -> backtest -> forward-test -> paper trade -> analyze -> improve, with no bookmaker, exchange or order-placement client anywhere in the repository. It separates REG, POST, WC, DS, LCS and WS environments (ALL is a roll-up view, not a blended score), carries 68 versioned strategy hypotheses with immutable strategy and model version records, and keeps an append-only SHA-256 hash-chained ledger protected by SQLite UPDATE and DELETE triggers. A source snapshot has now been loaded via content-addressed api.github.com git-blob fetches, taking the repository from its earlier NO_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT state to SOURCE_SNAPSHOT: 28,072 tracked games of which 27,972 are completed, 144,098 ledger records and 441 upcoming bets. Its defining behaviour survives that change intact — settled_bets is still 0 and total_simulated_pnl is still null, because the backtest gate requires a verified timestamped quote before anything can be staked, so the 144,098 records resolve to 118,214 EVAL (calibration only) and 25,884 PROPOSED rather than to profit. The odds source it did find is recorded as PARTIALLY_VERIFIED and marked ineligible for paper PnL specifically because it carries no observed_at, available_at or closing_flag field. All 18 adversarial audit controls pass.

value.description: Zero-dependency static MLB scoreboard that adds, for every game on a date's slate, the official weather picture at the ballpark and a verified record of every delay, postponement and suspension. Three pages (index.html scoreboard, delays.html all-games delay feed, game.html single game) read the MLB StatsAPI for status, gameInfo.delayDurationMinutes, play-by-play game_advisory events and box-score info labels, and the US National Weather Service (points -> hourly forecast -> active alerts) for weather, falling back to Environment and Climate Change Canada for Rogers Centre and to Open-Meteo elsewhere (always flagged non-government-source). Delay rows are produced only from official MLB status data, never from a forecast; the derived forecast-risk chip prints its own six thresholds (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/NONE/COVERED/UNKNOWN) verbatim from RISK_RULES in assets/js/weather.js. A captured copy of the full GET /api/v1/gameStatus registry holds 210 status rows, and three offline Node test suites assert 56 checks in total (26 delays, 24 weather, 6 render).

value.description: Autonomous NBA betting-strategy research and paper-trading competition lab that cross-verifies real public data, turns public claims into testable hypotheses, backtests them against verified historical prices where those exist and forward-tests them where they do not. Signal-quality results are published as signal quality and never mixed into backtest or forward PnL records. As of the generated leaderboard at 2026-09-21T19:58:05Z the competition has genuinely not started: all 22 forward entries read status 'awaiting-opportunity' with 0 bets and a null win rate, and all 22 backtest entries read 'no historical data' — the platform reports the absence rather than a zero. value.description: Simulated multi-sport parlay research platform and paper-trading competition across NFL, MLB, NHL and NBA — dependency-free Python engine, hash-routed static site, two sealed books that are accounted separately and never merged. State read from data/site/meta.json at commit f939267 (engine 1.1.0, exported 2026-09-22T20:06:21Z over data as of 2026-09-22T01:30:00Z): 29,056 games, 7,014 parlays, 20,570 legs and the same 20,570 signals, 8,267 ledger rows, 60,504 prices, 54,296 ratings, 28 strategies, 28 users, 24 research items, 28 verifications and 13 open quality issues. The catalog in parlaysports/strategies.py is 28 versioned strategies — six per sport plus four multi-sport — each with a named manager, a written hypothesis, selection rules, a minimum edge and documented limitations, staking 10 USD per ticket (the longshot lottery book 25 USD) from a 10,000 USD bankroll per strategy per book. Every leg and ticket carries a pricing grade: VERIFIED, REFERENCE, MODEL, MIXED or UNPRICED, the last tracked for hit rate only at 0 stake. Settlement is append-only from final scores, with push and void legs reducing a ticket and an all-push ticket refunded. Three gates were executed in this audit rather than quoted: the unittest suite ran 60 tests OK, the committed data/audit_report.json holds 63 checks every one of which is PASS, and node scripts/ui_smoke.mjs rendered all 15 site routes.
flags: The committed audit report is 63/63 PASS, but re-running scripts/audit.py from a fresh clone in this audit stopped at check 2 with 'database-exists: run seed first', because the working database is not committed. The 63/63 published here is the repository's own persisted record at this commit, not a gate this audit reproduced end to end; `make seed` has to run first. IRR-78.

Coverage gaps are declared rather than padded: the pinned MLB results file holds full 2023-2025 and Apr-Jul 2015 only, with nothing for 2016-2022, so MLB backtests run over 2023-2025 and a missing-historical-periods quality check flags the gap on every build. NBA backtests use Oct-Dec slices only from the SBR archive, S-NHL-05 has no verified puck-line history and is forward-armed only, S-MLB-06 is forward-only by design, and multi-sport backtests cover only measured cross-sport overlap slates.

MODEL-grade payouts are estimates from assumed -110 or proxy lines and are labelled as such; backtests assume closing-line availability and ignore line movement, limits and fees; multi-sport legs assume independence with no correlation model and there are no same-game parlays in v1; Kalshi prices exclude exchange fees; and player and game props are not simulated at all because no free verified historical prop feed exists.

Twelve inherited NBA rows were 0-0 'finals' for games that had been postponed: nine are verified against published postponement notices and three are recorded as not played with verified=0 and an explicit 'reason NOT independently verified' note. Postponed games are never settled and never rated, and a ticket leg on one is voided with its stake refunded.

A flat-stake book can exceed its starting bankroll on paper, which the repository states rather than hides: equity curves, drawdowns and bankroll reconciliation are computed in economic time from ledger amounts, and the integrity checks fail the run on a negative balance, a drawdown above 100 percent or any drift against the recorded current amount.

value.description: Open, auditable rebuild of the data quality behind RotoGrinders' DFS projection system: what it uses, where that data comes from, what could be verified from official sources and — equally — what could not. statement: MasterSite catalogs SelfLearn — Autonomous No-LLM Research Engine in Science & ML Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Autonomous research engine that will not publish a sentence it cannot quote from a document it actually retrieved, and that contains no language model anywhere in its pipeline: claims are spans cut out of retrieved documents and accepted or rejected by string and set operations anyone can re-run. It has no third-party dependencies at all, not even for HTTP or HTML, and requires Python 3.10 or newer. One cycle plans what to read, retrieves through a politeness- and budget-limited client, hashes and stores the response in evidence/snapshots/ before anything reads it, cuts candidate claims, verifies each against the stored document (numbers, dates, polarity, direction, universality, then quote match and token coverage), detects contradictions, lets six competing personas build answers out of verified claims only, attacks them with eleven named deterministic critic rules, ranks them on nine published criteria with Elo ratings accumulating across cycles, runs seeded experiments in a subprocess with a tamper check on the script hash, derives new questions and publishes everything as a static site plus machine-readable JSON. Library state read from reports/site_data.json at commit b787077 (generated 2026-09-22T23:12:31Z): 300 claims, 89 documents, 222 competing candidates carrying 960 recorded criticisms, 141 derived open questions, 12 contradictions awaiting a human decision, 102 discoveries, 4 topics, 22 recorded failures and 35 registered irregularities — 28 open (15 warning, 13 info, 0 error) and 7 resolved. The 156-test suite was executed in this audit and passed.

The engine reports its own gaps instead of filling them: checks.claims_without_link is 159 of 300 claims, unsupported_claims is 10, unresolved_contradictions is 12 with 0 resolved, fixture_documents is 0, and at the time of this read sources_polled was 1 with sources_reached 0 and the CLI printed 'no recorded cycle found in reports/site_data.json; the sources table shows no reachability'. statement: MasterSite catalogs ShoulderPain — Research-Backed Shoulder & Scapula Pain Guide in Health & Personal Guides; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Source-linked GitHub Pages guide to shoulder and shoulder-blade ('wing') pain, written around one stated context — a male adult aged about 36-40, left-side sleeping, a possible workout injury, prolonged computer use and limited room space — and explicitly educational information rather than a diagnosis or a personalised rehabilitation plan, with emergency and urgent warning signs given priority over exercises, furniture or symptom logging. Ten pages share one static template and compact navigation: start, medical advice, treatment, exercises, desk and room, furniture and prices, care costs, an optional log, sources and audit, and next steps; all research content works without JavaScript and no sign-in or symptom entry is required. The current revision is a deliberate narrowing rather than an expansion. It reviewed the pre-existing site at commit e1c63c4 and, in its own words, 'replaces blanket verification/completeness claims with a narrower, auditable source register, simplifies the UI and corrects unsafe or unverified assumptions', keeping the previous site in Git history. Twenty official pages were opened directly on 2026-09-20 — MedlinePlus, NHS, AAOS/ASES, CSP, OSHA, CMS, five furniture manufacturers or sellers, and Luna — and data/sources.json records each source's section, a short excerpt, its scope and its check date, with government and medical-society guidance kept separate from commercial product information. data/claims.json maps source-bearing content units to references and source-file lines: 90 review units, described as a review aid and 'not an automated truth certificate'. Exercises were reduced to four source-checked examples carrying exact AAOS HTML doses and supervision boundaries. Five furniture listings give exact variant and price boundaries with folding trade-offs, and no product is claimed to fit an unmeasured room or to treat shoulder pain; the one care price quoted is an official provider example ($135 self-pay per visit at Luna), not a nationwide average, and other unverified medical costs are explicitly left unpriced. REVIEW.md documents three passes and eight source irregularities found while reading, including a COMHOMA price where $54.49 was the selected White variant and $25.50 the discount, a VIVO desk that folds against the wall but is not quickly detached, a Lillipad whose specifications claim a 700 lb static test while its FAQ says 350 lb and neither replaces the 75 lb operational rating, and a Luna search excerpt showing $125 where both directly opened pages showed $135. The optional log is local-only, retains the `shoulderpain-log-v1` key so prior entries can still be read or imported if valid, and validates numbers, booleans, calendar dates and shape; invalid entries are counted and never rounded or silently converted, invalid persisted data blocks edits rather than being overwritten, raw JSON export is available for recovery, cross-tab changes block saves until reload, spreadsheet formula injection is mitigated on CSV export, and the bounded import size was raised to 20 MB so the 5,000-entry schema can import its own backups. Its former clinical 'improving/worsening' classifier and calendar-based advice were removed on the grounds that sparse logs should not reassure someone or postpone assessment, and the summary is now descriptive only. Validation reports 8 Node unit tests and 31 Chromium browser tests passing, automated axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 AA checks passing on all ten pages at 390px and 1440px, and no page-level horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768 or 1440px. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20.
flags: Its own verification policy refuses the strongest claims a directory reader might assume: 'Unknown or conflicting facts stay visibly unresolved. No claim of independent clinical verification or zero errors', and 'Automated checks cannot establish medical accuracy'. REVIEW.md adds that no clinician independently reviewed the personalised suitability of the information, and that link integrity, automated accessibility and browser tests are not medical validation.

Deliberately narrower than the version it replaced. The prior revision carried a 56-source register (S1-S56), four logged review passes, 32 logged corrections and a 32-row irregularity table; this one carries 20 opened sources, three passes, 8 source irregularities and a 6-row next-steps table. Its stated reason is worth quoting because it is the opposite of the usual instinct: 'The guide is a focused, source-linked starting set, not all possible diseases or products. Further expansion should improve evidence rather than inflate a count' (IRR-57).

Now has a build and test step, unlike the version previously described here: npm ci, npm run build (claim ledger plus ten static root HTML pages), npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser (Playwright) and npm run serve, with the shared page layout in tools/build.py and Python 3 and Node 22 used in validation. Visitors need neither. Committed root HTML means the Pages configuration needs no runtime build.

Browser tests were run against an npm-distributed Chromium 153 binary extracted outside Git because the standard Playwright browser download and Debian package retrieval were blocked by sandbox networking; REVIEW.md states plainly that 'this is not an unexecuted test claim', and CI uses the normal Playwright installation on GitHub-hosted runners. Remaining testing limits it names: no manual screen-reader-user audit, no cross-browser matrix, no third-party video-playback test, and automated accessibility is not full conformance certification.

Open limitations it lists for a next session: no clinician exam or clinical peer review and no systematic literature review; actual room fit, safe removal route and body/desk measurements unknown; no checked chair meets both the folding and the adjustable long-day-workstation criteria; product stock, prices and return policies change and Lillipad has contradictory page content; personal care and medicine costs, country and insurance remain unknown.

Changed state four times inside one audit and this description is the fourth rewrite — verified in sequence against 239eaa8 (01:25:47Z), dd1a7d4 (02:13:17Z), 6812ef3 (02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after a prior stamp had been written) and now 8a21b94 (03:07:51Z), which rebuilt all ten pages and reversed the sourcing method entirely (IRR-47, IRR-57).

Re-verified upstream on 21 September 2026: every medical, exercise and workstation source (M1-M6, E1-E3, W1-W3) was re-opened and all registered excerpts still match the official pages. Product rechecks succeeded only partially — VIVO and Lillipad were re-verified through official seller product-data endpoints, while fetch-proxy failures prevented re-opening IKEA, Branch, three manual/spec PDFs and the cost sources, whose entries stay dated 20 September 2026 and are labelled as such on the site. No price, stock or fit fact was invented for the items that could not be re-opened.

statement: MasterSite catalogs StockPaperSim — Persona Paper-Trading Competition (Replay + Live Book) in Markets & Trading Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: One-year paper-trading competition between return-seeking strategy personas, with a real venue model (depth, spreads, market making, dated tick sizes and fees), a full audit trail and a dependency-free static site. The repository documents three runs, re-read 2026-09-20 at its fourth pass: Season 1 with 20 personas replaying the real S&P 500 and VIX path (republished with its numbers re-derived rather than patched), the legacy Live Book with 19 personas trading forward from official free series (Nasdaq Composite, Dow Jones, S&P 500, VIX, SOFR and four macro series), and Season 2 with 19 personas in a reproducible research replay on collected daily bars — the Season 2 roster having grown from 14 to 19 with three new slate personas (NFL, NBA, NCAA) and two forward-only probes, while the landed complete ESPN NBA scoreboard (1,330 rows, 2025-10-21 to 2026-06-14) lets the NBA slate persona trade the full 2025-26 season. The fourth pass is the arrival of real SEC Form 4 insider data through an agent lane: a rendered-extraction campaign collected 65 filings and 99 parsed transactions across all ten tracked tickers (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, JPM, XOM, JNJ, PG, TSLA, MU, T), every filing dated on or after 2026-06-01, captured as the SEC's own XSL-rendered Form 4 views plus filing indexes through the page-fetch route into data/real/sec_agent/, whose 131-entry staged_manifest.json has every file SHA-256 digested and re-verified at staging. sim/edgar_rendered.py parses those captures fail-closed — handling footnoted codes and prices, dual and triple checkbox roles and 10b5-1 plan flags — and scripts/stage_sec_rendered.py integrates the lane into the same JSONL the walk and bulk sets feed, de-duplicated on (accession, date, ticker, code, shares, price). Eleven filings parse to no Table I trade rows because they are derivative-only DSU/RSU grants or balance-only rows, and are flagged rather than dropped silently. The gaps are recorded rather than hidden: two MU filings exceeded the page-fetch size budget and were excluded, and the window contains zero code-P open-market purchases, so the buy-side insider signals register as NO-OBSERVATIONS and @InsiderCluster_Live reports READY-NO-OBSERVATIONS — ready and reading real filings but placing no intents until purchases land. The quarterly structured bulk sets remain refused to the collection runner (HTTP 403 / rate gate, limitation L-27), so this is a complementary rendered lane, not a replacement. The suite is 648 tests green, the official audit report adds 1,871 checks, and the committed registers hold 78 irregularities and 44 limitations. It states plainly that the executable bars are collected Yahoo Finance files marked SECONDARY, that two of seventeen price series in Season 1 are real observations while the other fifteen are labelled simulations, and that the committed-price run is not eligible as an official-price competition. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20. A clean front-door hub was added at the repository root this pass and docs/ was regenerated from the current generator to close a stale-site gate.

Its insider signal is ready but has nothing to trade on. The extracted Form 4 window contains zero code-P open-market purchases, so @InsiderCluster_Live reports READY-NO-OBSERVATIONS and the insider participants hold no positions and say why, rather than substituting an aggregator for a filing or showing an empty result as a neutral one. Two MU filings were excluded for exceeding the page-fetch size budget, and 11 of the 65 parse to no Table I trade rows — all flagged, none dropped silently.

Data provenance is labelled rather than smoothed: the executable bars are collected Yahoo Finance files marked SECONDARY, only two of seventeen Season 1 price series are real observations with the other fifteen labelled simulations, and the committed-price run is explicitly not eligible as an official-price competition. The SEC quarterly structured bulk sets are still refused to its runner (HTTP 403 / rate gate, L-27).

Fast-moving repository: a single-commit README-only placeholder in the 2026-09-17 audit, it needed description rewrites in each audit since — the Season 2 roster went 14 to 19 personas (IRR-37), then the fourth pass landed the SEC Form 4 agent lane and moved tests 634 to 648, audit checks 1,870 to 1,871 and LIMITATIONS.json 43 to 44 (IRR-61). The data-quality argument is that matching Stokastic requires five layers — official league stats, Vegas and sportsbook lines, contextual injury and weather data, DFS-specific structure with salary caps of 50K on DraftKings and 60K on FanDuel, and advanced derived values such as Value = FP minus Salary/1000 times 5. docs/index.html is a 71,004-byte static site carrying 155 verified badges.

Everything proprietary is labelled inference rather than reproduced: exact projection weights are not published and the engine uses minutes 40 percent, usage 25 percent, matchup 20 percent, recent form 10 percent and other 5 percent; historical ownership is private and proxied with optimal percent plus salary; the correlation matrix is a heuristic (0.6 QB-WR, 0.3 WR-WR) rather than a measured joint distribution; the demo simulator's contest payout curve is illustrative; and the pricing page is coupon-gated and seasonally dynamic, so both toggles were recorded on 2026-09-22 with a note that a manual reviewer should re-fetch it live.

value.description: Reproducible research layer for TradingView's The Leap paper-trading competition (AMP Futures, Sep 2026) that separates official contest facts, historical champion outcomes, vendor-sourced market moves, capacity arithmetic and independently simulated strategy verdicts — and never presents a backtest as a platform result. Its 2026-09-20 audit banner reports that the volatile-stock matrix is now COMPLETE: 60/60 series captured (20 x 15m + 20 x 1h + 20 x 1d) through a CI capture lane with byte-level SHA-256 provenance, recorded in data/intraday_index.json, up from the 37/60 partial pool (16 x 15m, 10 x 1h, 11 x 1d) reported two days earlier. Full-pool verdicts were assigned at 60/60: H34 and H37 partially supported, H36 supported, H35 and H38 refuted, H39 (C19) and H41 (C22) inconclusive on zero fire; the pre-registered gate then fired and the new variant C19-A was registered as H42, also zero-fire and therefore inconclusive on its first full-pool run. The banner is equally explicit about what the captures are not: they are Yahoo vendor-tier, not exchange-verified; the Alpaca IEX route (`make official-bars`) remains blocked on environment credentials; and no authenticated TradingView Strategy Report export is available. The body's latest pass section is still the September 19 sixteenth pass, whose verified facts are unchanged: the tenth official frontier capture (R10, N=99,663) recorded the edition's first rank-1 turnover, with HappyLittleTrades promoted from #3 to rank 1 at +994.30 percent / $2,485,745.50 and youcanttrickme falling to #4 at +908.01 percent / $2,270,023.00, and ranks 1-250 fully re-enumerated into committed evidence; the rules were re-verified line by line with 94/94 symbols, caps and listing order identical and 0 equity instruments; all 15 completed-edition champion records were re-read verbatim with 0 mismatch, the maximum being 53.2072x, so no 100x appears in verified history; the $50,000 cash ARV prize ladder is unchanged; and the frozen model roster grew 32 to 38 with C17 (overnight implosion harvester), C18 (blow-off short avalanche) and C19 (twin-hammer capitulation compounder) added alongside hypotheses H37-H39, daily usernames 28 to 34. Verification at that pass ran 401 passed / 0 failed / 1 warning, a 459-check self-test and 94 unit tests. One text change was found in the rules and flagged rather than silently adopted: the payment rail moved from 'at least $1000 wire-or-PayPal' to 'at least $600 wire-only' (IR-29, low), with the payout configuration left frozen at the $1000 reading. Placement arithmetic still holds that matching rank 50 from a fresh $250,000 account needs +15.99 percent per day compounded, unbroken. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20. Since that banner the pool has moved again: a nineteenth contrarian model, C23 (serial capitulation snapback), was pre-registered as H43 after a documented pre-freeze probe of 75 eight-streaks pool-wide and was refuted on its first full-pool run — both usernames beat the control over 81 season editions, but the forward held-out split missed by $20.56 — that figure and the 196-date roll schedule below are quoted from the README audit banner at the stamped commit 5b14c89 and both have since been superseded at head d09a594 (IRR-91). CME product hours for all 20 pooled futures are now committed with a 196-date roll schedule (18 codecs, 2 refusals). Captures remain Yahoo vendor-tier rather than exchange-verified: the Alpaca IEX route stays blocked on environment credentials, and the repository states plainly that no figure on the site is claimed to come from a real TradingView Strategy result.
flags: Its own banner states the limit plainly: captures are Yahoo vendor-tier, NOT exchange-verified, official intraday acquisition is credential-blocked, the Alpaca IEX route needs authorized environment credentials, and no authenticated TradingView Strategy Report export exists. 'Do not treat historical candidates as current orders.'

The README's header banner and its body are out of step. The banner is dated 2026-09-20 and reports the completed 60/60 matrix, models C22 and C19-A and hypotheses H41 and H42, but those identifiers appear nowhere else in the document — the newest body section is still 'September 19 sixteenth pass', whose roster is 32 to 38 with C17-C19 and H37-H39, and whose audit banner note still describes the 37/60 partial pool. A reader taking the roster count or the verdict list from the body gets the previous state (IRR-59).

Most full-pool verdicts are negative or non-results rather than wins: H35 and H38 refuted, H34 and H37 only partially supported, and H39, H41 and H42 inconclusive because their models never fired on the full pool. A zero-fire model is reported as inconclusive, not as a pass.

Contest facts are re-verified rather than remembered, and discrepancies are registered instead of smoothed: the landing hero count (99,658) trails the contest count (99,663) by the usual async lag (IR-09), and the payment-rail text change is flagged as IR-29 with the payout config deliberately left at the older reading.
Read at commit 6d8f0ef, its fourth move inside two audits; the previous three were recorded at IRR-36 when the description was rewritten from R9 (96,707 participants) to R10 (99,663).

statement: MasterSite catalogs VacationSchedule — Free Time Scoreboard (SF Radio Blackout Calendar) in Sports Data & Scoreboards; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Bay Area vacation planner comparing three definitions of sports-free time in 2026-2029 for a listener in San Francisco ZIP 94122, with one-, two- and three-week trip checks, a daily scoreboard, a month calendar, Pacific-time free intervals, sources and a review queue. The three sections nest: Section 1 counts all 30 MLB clubs plus 49ers preseason, regular season and postseason and the Westwood One national NFL feeds as busy; Section 2 adds Stanford and California football; Section 3 adds San Jose Earthquakes MLS. An 'Everything tracked' option adds national NCAA football plus Golden State Warriors and Golden State Valkyries on KGMZ 95.7 The Game. Only AM/FM broadcasts count, so the San Jose Sharks (app/streaming only) and Audacy-app-only Valkyries games are disclosed exclusions, and USF basketball, Westwood One NCAA basketball and local college basketball are named as documented gaps rather than silently treated as free time. With Spring Training excluded, Sections 1 and 2 give longest modeled windows of 44 days in 2026 (Feb 9 - Mar 24, past), 37 in 2027 (Feb 15 - Mar 23), 40 in 2028 (estimated) and 41 in 2029 (estimated); with Spring Training included no section reaches two weeks. The repository refuses a blanket verified claim: TBD kickoff reserves the entire local date including DST 23- and 25-hour days, 'no known conflict' is stated to describe the snapshot rather than certify a quiet day, and all times are America/Los_Angeles rather than a fixed UTC-8 offset. A 2026-09-21 session-3 pass added two tabs: MLB 2026 & 2027, listing every fixture the league has scheduled for all 30 clubs from the committed Stats API snapshot with each row carrying the league's own game_pk, and Postseason 2026, which splits the postseason into what is resolved and what is not — clinched berths and division titles, official round dates, dates that cannot carry a game, and a machine-measured count of published first pitches, still zero. The fixture lists are produced on a GitHub runner by scripts/export_mlb_schedule.py, validated for all 30 clubs, a plausible regular-season count and unique game ids, and committed with a provenance summary recording the exact request URL, the retrieval time and a SHA-256 of the raw response, so every row is re-verifiable by hand. Where a season snapshot exists the analysis blocks real fixture dates rather than a continuous season frame.
flags: Substantially rewritten upstream between 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 (13 commits, 'Rebuild site as a clean, table-first vacation decision engine'). The previously published description — 11-day best window, 42 tests, 53 review items, 21 irregularities in docs/IRREGULARITIES.md — no longer matches the repository and has been replaced wholesale rather than patched (IRR-66).

Classification changed stub -> app: the Pages workflow publishes site/ via Actions, and the repository also commits a root index.html that forwards to site/ so the legacy main/root Pages setting keeps working. tools/audit_kind.py now reports main//index.html HTTP 200, resolving the earlier IRR-43-class finding.

Coverage is explicitly partial and the repository says so: the 2026-09-21 pass re-verified Westwood One rows, MLB clinch facts, Super Bowl dates and the 49ers per-game radio stations, but college and MLS fixtures remain inherited snapshots, and 53 postseason records still have no published start time.

statement: MasterSite catalogs Commodities — Kalshi Research Exchange in Markets & Trading Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Evidence-first paper-trading lab for Kalshi event contracts, organised around an automated forward-test desk. 28 live return-seeking strategy personas plus 2 deliberately gated ones (Form4Flash, SpreadSmith) trade open Kalshi contracts on paper from a scheduled, read-only GitHub Actions collector — a cheap tick every five minutes aimed at in-game markets and a full cycle twice an hour at :07 and :37 — and every fill, exit, settlement, intent, mark and order book is committed back to the repository. Two backtests run on verified official Kalshi price data: the original hand-collected sample (3 settled markets, 130 verified bars, 5 personas), deliberately frozen, and an archive backtest replayed bar by bar over the candle archive the collector now stores, with per-trade equity curves and a walk-forward stability split. An execution-realism check re-reads every simulated fill against Kalshi's own published trade tape via GET /markets/trades and reports the difference in cents, with a committed live result of 156 fills compared at a median absolute desk-minus-tape gap of 1.00 cent, 74.36 percent within 1 cent of a real print, 69.23 percent inside the tape's real range and 65.38 percent covered by tape volume. A season health audit (scripts/audit_season.py) checks the schedule, ledger coverage, storage compaction, signal adapters and the tape summary, re-reads settled markets against the official API on the runner, and refuses to let verify_data.py pass if anything disagrees. Simulation only: nothing submits orders to Kalshi and no API key exists anywhere in the project. IRREGULARITY: the README's own archive-backtest headline (63 markets, 2,455 verified bars, 291 trades) does not match the committed generated files at the same head, which hold 74 markets, 2,736 verified bars and 337 trade rows across 266 distinct trade ids; both sets of figures are published here and the generated files are the number of record (IRR-97).
flags: Newly added this pass: HeatConfirm, a weather rule discovered in a third-party Reddit backtest post, is traded forward precisely because its backtest claim is someone else's — the repository labels the source discovery-only and never a price source, and testing the claim forward IS the experiment.

The desk quantifies its own cron reliability rather than assuming it: IRR-34 (2026-09-21) records scripts/audit_season.py counting every scheduled :07/:37 UTC slot against committed cycles, and the committed audit shows 4 cycles with API errors out of 361 evidence-bound ledger events.
Persona count moved 20 -> 23 and the source registry 63 -> 70 entries between the 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 audits; treat all counts here as point-in-time.

A season-rollover layer landed during this audit ('Extend evidence-first desk across archive and season rollover'), adding data/seasons.json, a per-strategy JSON page set, an audit history log and browser plus smoke tests for the rollover path. It changed none of the published figures above.

value.description: Product-only coupon, rebate and BOGO directory for the San Francisco Bay Area, re-scoped on 2026-09-22 to drop event tickets and museum admissions (49 venue-admission entries moved to archive/rescoped-2026-09-22/ with their reasoning, per the dataset's own scope_history). State read from the repository's own generated data/coupons.json at commit 7a130e1 (built_at 2026-09-22T23:43:31Z): 227 verified offers, 20 documented rejections, 265 citations across 72 distinct source domains, verification levels A 190 / B 34 / C 3, and 613 irregularity flags (20 critical, 497 warning, 96 info). Offers live in 15 curated JSON shards under data/entries/ — the largest, 01-pg-brandsaver.json, holding 112 transcribed P&G brandSAVER coupons — and carry 13 deal types. Sourcing is enforced by the build, not by convention: an aggregator, promo-code site, listicle or social domain cited as the source of an available offer fails the build, as does a citation with no verbatim evidence passage, publisher, access date and retrieval method. Expiry status is computed in the browser against the visitor's own date (Active to Expires soon at 7 days or fewer, to Expired, plus Window closed and Not redeemable yet), and every dated record carries a project-side recheck_due date set to the printed expiry minus a 3-day safety margin, which a weekly CI job uses to file re-verification issues before an offer goes stale. The suite now reports 56 tests (53 at the previous read), executed here with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: Ran 56 tests, OK.

The counted value 53 is what this entry publishes and the disagreement is registered as IRR-73 rather than resolved by picking one.

The README's category table (113 manufacturer-digital, 16 restaurant-loyalty, 14 local-independent, 13 bogo-multi-buy, 13 manufacturer-printable, 12 no-spend-free and so on) sums to 213 across 185 offers because categories are multi-valued tags, not a partition: data/coupons.json's own stats.entries_by_category reproduces exactly those numbers. Do not read the table as summing to the offer count.

Freshness is bounded and the repository says so itself: the 112 P&G brandSAVER coupons carried printed expiries of 26-28 September 2026 and the site retires them automatically from those dates, while on the fifth research pass kellanovaus.com intermittently served its coupon grid unpopulated to a plain fetch, so its 8 printables could not be re-confirmed in that cycle — flagged by the repository rather than treated as retracted.

Personalised programmes (Safeway for U, Target Circle, Costco Instant Savings, restaurant apps) are verified at programme level only because their offers are per-account and cannot be read anonymously, and no Facebook or Instagram post was read or cited at all: both require authentication, so social platforms generated leads that were then verified on an official domain or rejected.

statement: MasterSite catalogs DrugAnalysis — FDA Decisions & Biotech Reactions in Markets & Trading Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Biopharma decision engine tracking publicly traded companies against FDA drug decisions, verified stock-price reactions and clinical-pipeline success rates, rendered as a dependency-free static site with no build step. The project is now at v29 (2026-09-22) and the whole-table census has landed: the official Drugs@FDA Submissions.txt holds 193,810 rows, and the boundary the project defends holds over all of them — 0 rows are dated between the FD&C Act (1938-06-25) and 1938-12-31. That census also contradicted two of the project's own v28 working hypotheses and v29 publishes the contradictions verbatim rather than smoothing them: the before-1939 window holds 1 row rather than 0 (ApplNo 060904, ORIG 1, AP, dated 1900-01-01, a pre-statute placeholder published as FLAG-PRE-STATUTE-DATE with counted_as_fda_decision false), the undated window holds 8 rows (1 ORIG on 009658 plus 7 SUPPL) enumerated as FLAG-UNDATED-ROW, and the arithmetic 193,810 = 1 + 8 + 193,801 is stated in the artifact. The status census over the complete table is AP 192,604 / TA 1,205 / empty 1 — not the AP-only census v28 expected — with TA defined verbatim from FDA's own Drugs@FDA glossary as a tentative approval that does not allow marketing, so the project's wording was refined from 'approval actions only' to 'approval-family actions only (AP, TA)'; the type census is ORIG 27,862 / SUPPL 165,948 and the builder now aborts on any status outside {AP, TA, empty}. ApplNos 060904 and 009658 have no row in the official Applications table in either publication, appear in no committed window and in no project table, and render no application section on their official overview pages — no cause is inferred. Two corrections are recorded as corrections, not as footnotes: v28 wrote that NDA000159 was already counted in data/pre1965_fda_decisions.csv, which was false (that table holds NME-comparable rows only, earliest 1942, and NDA000159 is row PRE1965AUDIT-1939-02 of the pre-1965 originals audit table), and the same error class had already been caught for NDA000004 in v28. A runner defect that made Actions runs 32 and 33 fail was found and fixed: zip_extract re-downloaded the official ZIP on every run and overwrote the SHA-pinned window extracts, so every SHA-gated builder aborted and the workflow's if: always() commit step pushed the drifted payloads to the feature branch after the PR had merged; zip_extract now honours skip_existing and a run that produces only skipped-existing stubs leaves manifest.json byte-identical, and a failed page-0 fetch in the paged openFDA kinds no longer writes a 0-record payload with status 200 over the committed file. The layers the previous version of this entry described still stand and are re-quoted: 1,215 rows in the full 1938-1964 submission register (850 ORIG/AP originals plus 365 SUPPL/AP supplements, every one of them submission_status AP — 0 RE and 0 W rows, because the official Submissions.txt publishes approval actions only and refused/withdrawn decisions are simply not obtainable from that source for any year, so the project's non-approval evidence is FDA's separate 458-letter CRL database), and the v26 census of 535 original approvals for 1939-1964 cross-checked against the full official database map of 29,336 applications with 0 absent, 0 application-type mismatches and 0 holder mismatches. scripts/validate_data.py was executed here and reports PASS: schema, IDs, dates, ranges and source URL checks succeeded.
flags: Moving faster than this directory can snapshot: DrugAnalysis advanced v21.1 -> v26 -> v27 across three of this audit's own build passes, the last landing while the audit was running. Every count here is a point-in-time read at commit 0d2dbcd.

The repository publishes verified negatives as first-class results rather than omissions: 1938 gets a row in data/pre1938_determination.csv recording that 1,216 official submission rows were searched and 0 exist for that year, and FDA's own series publishes 1938-40 only combined.

statement: MasterSite catalogs FLABSENGY — FantasyLabs Projection Reverse Engineering in Sports Data & Scoreboards; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Clean-room study of the FantasyLabs DFS projection system plus an original Python engine that rebuilds the metrics the vendor documents publicly — no subscription data, no scraped pages, no proprietary weights, and an explicit record of what was refused. Evidence counted at commit f927bab: docs/ledger.html holds 49 source rows inside an S1-S50 range, research/IRREGULARITIES.md carries 16 flagged items I1-I16, research/REQUIREMENTS.md maps acceptance requirements R1-R17, and engine/fantasylab_engine/metrics.py defines 14 functions covering Plus/Minus, implied points from a salary-expectation fit, Pts/Sal, consistency, upside, duds, bargain rating, opponent Plus/Minus, salary change and percentile rank. `pytest -q` was executed in this audit and returned 79 passed. Where the vendor's own official glossaries disagree — the NFL defines Duds as fewer than half a salary-based expectation while the NBA and MLB glossaries define it as at least half a standard deviation below it — the engine implements both variants and documents which one is the default; where a methodology is not public at all (ownership projection, Pro Trend definitions, salary-regression parameters) it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
flags: Two of the README's headline counts are off against the files they describe. Its table says '50 sources' where docs/ledger.html holds 49 rows — the ledger states in terms that 'Missing ID S15 is reserved (not used)' — and 'All 19 publicly documented metrics' where docs/metrics.html carries 20 metric rows. This entry publishes the counted values 49 and 20; the disagreement is IRR-74.

The refusals are the substance of the audit, not an omission from it: I1-I3 record that the request to rebuild whatever sits behind the paywall would be paywall circumvention and reproduction of copyrighted subscription content, and that the Terms governing fantasylabs.com ban scraping, robots and reverse engineering of source code. The repository therefore limited itself to a handful of direct public page reads and wrote the engine from published metric definitions.

Two live findings about the vendor are reported and deliberately not exploited: fantasylabs.com/articles-new/ is publicly reachable and labelled '(Test)' in a search index (I10), and a search index surfaced a raw JSON player-news API path that appeared to need no authentication (I11). The endpoint was not interrogated further and is not consumed.

FanDuel scoring is taken from the operator's own rules page against secondary DFS guides that claim FanDuel has no yardage bonuses (I12); the engine trusts official pages only and excludes the secondary tables from its config.

All 10 verification anomalies are the same check, instrument_present_in_published_universe — instruments that settled and dropped out of the universe file. They are reported on the site and never silently corrected.

Of the 6 documented backtest rules only two recorded any trades at all (Metals Settlement Trend 674 and Channel Breakout 20/10 on MOEX metals 143); the other four recorded 0. statement: MasterSite catalogs GEMSDOE — Geologic Mapping Prize Challenge in Science & ML Research; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Evidence-backed working site for the DOE GEMS Prize Challenge on DrivenData — predicting geothermal faults in the GeoDAWN region under a distance-weighted Tversky metric, with a 19-band feature stack, a $300,000 prize pool split $50,000 initial and $250,000 final, ending 2026-12-03 at 11:59 p.m. UTC. STATUS.md at commit cf20e1b records session 23 (2026-09-22), which made it possible to generate a submission from the site itself in the browser with no install and no GPU: scripts/build_submission_payload.py encodes the adopted artifact into docs/submission_field.bin (a gems-rle-v1 uleb128 run-length stream, 532,174 bytes for 259,549 runs) with a manifest of grid, transform, EPSG, resolution, value counts, blob hash, artifact hash and 17 named checks, where --check re-derives the manifest from the raster and refuses if any pin drifted and --verify decodes the blob and compares float32 bits; docs/geotiff_writer.js is a dependency-free TIFF/ZIP writer in plain JS with real deflate, and the CLI and CI routes produce the same bytes. Session 21 closed the standing data-placement blocker in-sandbox: scripts/assemble_data_bridge.py reassembled all three official rasters from committed parts in 2.8 s with every part and whole-file sha256 verified (training_features.tif 418,912,844 B, labels.tif 425,830 B, sample_submission.tif 1,599,597 B), and scripts/prepare_data.py passed on the placed bytes (3292x3730, 19 bands, EPSG:32611, 100 m, aligned bounds, band tags present); scripts/baseline_submission.py then reproduced the committed submission.tif byte for byte (sha256 9f2577cff20d...) in about 17 minutes on 2 vCPU with no torch, and scripts/validate_submission.py passed all 8 checks on the fresh file. The scientific stance remains deliberately unhedged and unclaimed: all four block-holdout folds are committed and the memorisation-versus-transfer gap is reported as a spread rather than a point — fold 0 +0.0114, fold 1 -0.0070, fold 2 +0.0139, fold 3 +0.0093, mean +0.006904, spread 0.020935, positive in 3 of 4 — and because no fold reaches the 12 resampling units a readable block-bootstrap interval needs, the scorer itself flags every per-fold interval interval_readable false, so the honest reading is 'no clear memorisation, no clear transfer gain' with the full-grid 0.099859 (reproduced digit-for-digit on a runner) retained as the selection statistic. The pseudo-label contrast has fired twice and STATUS.md is explicit that quoting either fire alone would overstate the precision: the first gave held-out blocks 0.0806 to 0.1841 (+0.1036, P=0.999) on the new-fault-like proxy against 0.2113 to 0.1239 (-0.0874, P=0.001) on catalogue labels, and the second — same seed, same config, same partition, different runner — measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue -0.1079, a roughly 0.036 run-to-run swing on the proxy arm of the same order as the +0.0313 union contrast itself; the two scopes also disagree in sign on the union (+0.0313 held-out against -0.0375 trained-on), which STATUS.md calls instability rather than a result. Against the paired block-bootstrap bar its own FIELD rule uses (P >= 0.95) the union contrast reaches P = 0.916 with an interval spanning zero on 8 scoreable blocks, so it is suggestive and not established, both verdicts carry shippable_evidence false, and the circularity is derived rather than asserted because the pseudo-label path is the same proxy_catalogue.tif the proxy truth is cut from. A third population is the disjoint 122,652-pixel union (60,988 + 61,664, disjointness verified at score time). STATUS.md also defuses one coincidence on purpose: the baseline's union held-out DTI of 0.197183 resembles the public leaderboard's top score of 0.1972, and the two are unrelated quantities. IRREGULARITY: the repository's own test suite fails at this head — `python3 -m pytest tests -q` gives 467 passed, 32 skipped and 1 FAILED (tests/test_site_pages.py::test_the_build_reproduces_the_committed_pages), and 32 of the skips are environment-gated rather than the 1 STATUS.md reports (IRR-102). The next-session ordering stands at item 8 (the only unbiased signal: enroll and first upload, against a bar of 0.2854 as of 2026-09-21), then 3, then 6, then firing the pseudo-label workflow for folds 1-3 so the pool crosses 12 units before the runner artifacts expire around 2026-10-03.
flags: Repository size measured at 398,785 KB on the 2026-09-20 audit (6,695 KB on 2026-09-16 before the competition rasters were committed as sha256-pinned git parts, 394,791 KB on 2026-09-17, 395,958 KB on 2026-09-18). GitHub has not recomputed it since despite roughly 180,000 lines of new JSON evidence landing in session 19, which is the asynchronous-`size` behaviour IRR-04 to IRR-06 describe.

The README warns that its own earlier text is partly superseded (the feature stack is 19 bands, not ~10) and that STATUS.md and the generated site take precedence — this description is therefore sourced from STATUS.md, not the README body.
Canonical generated site lives in docs/ behind a root redirect; both prize phases score a new fault dataset that is disjoint from the training labels.

Session numbering moves fast: STATUS.md's own header covers sessions 11-19 and this description was written against session 19 at commit 3093c6b, having been written against session 18 at c129336 earlier in the same audit. It records the repository's most self-critical finding yet — that a positive pseudo-label result was measured on the population the pseudo-labels were cut from, and that two component populations pointing in opposite directions settle nothing.

value.description: Evidence-led research into LineStar's DFS projection product (linestarapp.com): a dated review of the vendor's own public product descriptions, an independent data-and-implementation plan, and a runnable projection prototype over synthetic data. The repository states in terms what it is not — not a recovered private algorithm, not a subscription bypass, not a production sports-data service, not a legal clearance and not a demonstrated match to LineStar's data quality — and its research snapshot is dated 2026-09-22 UTC with the note that build dates do not reset source observation dates. Every count here was read from the committed evidence register at 66d9c9b and re-confirmed by running the repository's own validator: 36 capability records (public claim, evidence references, sport and screen scope, access status, independent implementation status, required inputs, limitations), 30 source records distinguishing vendor, league, government, provider, platform and community-maintainer, each with an observation date, short excerpt, location, link and excerpt hash; 62 line-referenced legacy claim groups correcting the previous state of this repository against the immutable base commit 0ac0b07a; a 13-label coverage plan, nine input categories, 14 review flags, 10 findings and six prioritized next-work packages. `npm run check` was executed in this audit and passed all three of its gates: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` reported 72 tests, 72 pass, 0 fail on Node v22.22.3; `scripts/validate.mjs` printed 'Traceability valid: 36 capabilities, 30 sources, 62 legacy review groups. This is not automated proof of source truth.'; and `scripts/build.mjs --check` printed 'Verified 22 deterministic site assets. Both main:/ and main:/docs entrypoints are supported.' A further 13 Playwright browser and accessibility specs exist in tests/browser/ and were not executed, because no browser binary is available in this audit environment. The published site is a 217,302-byte root index.html built from web/template.html with search, category and evidence filtering, deep citations, JSON and CSV downloads and no-JavaScript research content; the prototype is a deterministic lab doing recency-weighted mean forecasts, point-in-time filtering, historical quantiles, an exact small-pool lineup solver, locks and exclusions, optional QB stack, greedy multi-lineup diversity and exposure constraints, late-swap slot preservation, stale-data blocking and safe CSV export, evaluated walk-forward on fixtures with EV arithmetic from assumed rather than estimated probabilities.
