statement: MasterSite catalogs MLB Live PBP — Scoreboard & Play-by-Play in Sports Data & Scoreboards; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Zero-dependency static web app that pulls live MLB game data straight from the public MLB StatsAPI and renders it in a Gameday-style scoreboard, re-implemented from scratch in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no build step, no frameworks and no API keys. Two views: a scoreboard showing every game for any date with live scores, inning, count, probable pitchers and W/L/S decisions, and a game view showing who is at bat, who is pitching, the count, outs, runners on base, on-deck and in-the-hole hitters, pitch counts, last play, inning-by-inning linescore, full box score and the complete play-by-play timeline with pitch-by-pitch detail. A third surface is devoted to replay: an all-games Replay Feed page pulls review events from every game on the schedule — manager challenges, crew chief reviews, umpire reviews and ABS pitch challenges — with game link, inning, challenging team, reason, outcome, batter/pitcher context and a three-row review score tracker (Before review, Possible after, Actual after) that explicitly refuses to treat the possible score as a prediction, marks Before/Possible as not observed when the page opens only after resolution, and never assigns a later end-of-plate-appearance score to an earlier pitch review. A Runs at Risk mechanism decides from the data rather than the review type whether the call on the field credited runs to the very event under review — a run counts only when the official payload has a runners[] record with details.isScoringEvent true whose details.playIndex matches the reviewed event — and fires once per review with a chime, an optional desktop notification and a persistent banner, never predicting the ruling. Review detection reads the API's own status registry rather than matching the words challenge/review, because that missed crew-chief reviews whose official detailedState is 'Instant Replay'. The challenge counters are the official StatsAPI counters read as-is (review.away/home.used/remaining and gameData.absChallenges.away/home), never counts derived from feed events, never zero-filled when absent, and a used-counter that moves backwards between polls is flagged on the row as an irregularity instead of being silently corrected. A two-sided hit forecast compounds the batter's and pitcher's season rates by log5 with real platoon splits, recent form, head-to-head history, same-game familiarity and the live count into a single probability with a matchup tier and per-driver point adjustments. Auto-refresh runs at 500ms for the full feed with a 250ms status watcher for the whole slate, and a lean play-by-play probe at 250ms while a review is in flight. LIMITATION: the offline test suites run here — 14 of the 15 tools/*-test.mjs suites pass — but tools/smoke-test.mjs reports 8 checks failed in this sandbox because it fetches the live statsapi.mlb.com teams directory, gameStatus registry and review-status projection and this audit environment has no egress to that host, so that result is an environment limit rather than evidence of a repository defect.

statement: MasterSite catalogs MLB Plaintext Play-by-Play Viewer in Sports Data & Scoreboards; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Searchable web viewer and reproducible archive pipeline for MLB regular-season and postseason games from 2014 forward, using exactly one source: HTTPS responses from MLB's own statsapi.mlb.com domain. It does not invent, estimate, silently repair or manually enter a score, name, play or measurement — the raw download is the exact official response body and the human-readable files are deterministic projections of fields in that response. It browses the official schedule by date and includes MLB sportId=1 game types R, F, D, L and W (regular season and postseason) while excluding Spring Training, exhibitions and the All-Star Game, renders line scores, decisions, every play, pitch and action details, runner movements and batting and pitching box scores, searches a game's official descriptions and player names in the browser, and downloads a readable .txt report, the complete raw .json or an event-oriented .ndjson without a server or account. A bulk archive runs from January 1, 2014 through any requested end date with retries, rate limiting, resume support, provenance checks and checksums, live games refresh automatically using the wait interval returned in MLB's feed, and while a game is Live the pipeline logs transient official events — score changes, official-scorer ruling changes, scoring-pending rulings and boundary calls — into a per-game Event log tab stored locally in the browser so it can be reopened after the event or the game is over. A response is accepted only if the URL is HTTPS on the exact statsapi.mlb.com host, the response is successful JSON, it contains MLB Advanced Media's provenance notice, and a game feed's returned gamePk matches the requested gamePk. The site has no sample scores and no fallback dataset: if the official endpoint cannot be reached or does not return a value, the interface says so. The repository does not relicense MLB data — every saved record keeps MLB Advanced Media's returned notice, the exact source URL, the UTC retrieval time and a SHA-256 digest, and users remain responsible for complying with MLB's terms. The site is dependency-free static HTML, CSS and JavaScript in docs/ that requests data directly from MLB in the visitor's browser, with no third-party analytics, proxy, database, generated game content, logo or team artwork. Both test suites were executed here: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` reports Ran 6 tests, OK, and `node --test tests/test_eventlog.mjs` reports 15 tests, 15 pass, 0 fail.

statement: MasterSite catalogs MLB Rain Delay — Live Scoreboard with Weather & Delay Tracking in Sports Data & Scoreboards; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Dependency-free static MLB rain-delay and postponement tracker and research site that cross-references the public MLB StatsAPI schedule with official NWS point, hourly forecast and alerts JSON (or the Environment Canada equivalent for Toronto) plus a documented list of stadium roof/retractable-roof facts, and labels every game's delay risk by a published rule rather than a guess. It covers the full official gameStatus registry — all 210 status codes captured verbatim in the fixtures — maps status.detailedState / statusCode / reason to High / Moderate / Low / None / Covered / Unknown with thresholds spelled out in RISK_RULES so a reviewer can re-derive every label, and lists 13 club pages with 11 named deficiencies (warm-weather bias, no surface/drainage field, market prices no single source publishes, and so on). One mode classifies a schedule; the other reclassifies an already-observed delay or postponement and measures the retrospective recall and precision of the prospective label on committed verified delays — never the other way round — and the site states plainly that a positive calibration result is not a validated operational delay-forecasting model. The social/headline layer is explicitly a flag-for-review aid that only fires when a news headline's verbatim title or description contains a word from the documented DELAY_WORDS / WEATHER_WORDS lists, recording the matched word, and it never asserts a delay. IRREGULARITY: the repository's own test suites have grown past the figures its documentation still prints. Executed here with node: tools/delays-test.mjs 32 passed, tools/weather-test.mjs 25 passed and tools/render-test.mjs 9 passed (66 across the three suites this entry's previous version named), with tools/news-test.mjs 25 passed and tools/match-test.mjs 18 passed also green — while docs/verification.md still reports '67 assertions across four suites (26 + 24 + 11 + 6)' and README.md still reports '100+ passing assertions' (IRR-103).

value.description: Simulated multi-sport parlay research platform and paper-trading competition across NFL, MLB, NHL and NBA — dependency-free Python engine, hash-routed static site, two sealed books that are accounted separately and never merged. The catalog in parlaysports/strategies.py is 28 versioned strategies — six per sport plus four multi-sport — each with a named manager, a written hypothesis, selection rules, a minimum edge and documented limitations, staking 10 USD per ticket (the longshot lottery book 25 USD) from a 10,000 USD bankroll per strategy per book. Every leg and ticket carries a pricing grade: VERIFIED, REFERENCE, MODEL, MIXED or UNPRICED, the last tracked for hit rate only at 0 stake. Settlement is append-only from final scores, with push and void legs reducing a ticket and an all-push ticket refunded. Three gates were executed in this audit rather than quoted: the unittest suite ran 60 tests OK, the committed data/audit_report.json holds 63 checks every one of which is PASS, and node scripts/ui_smoke.mjs rendered all 15 site routes.
flags: The committed audit report is 63/63 PASS, but re-running scripts/audit.py from a fresh clone in this audit stopped at check 2 with 'database-exists: run seed first', because the working database is not committed. The 63/63 published here is the repository's own persisted record at this commit, not a gate this audit reproduced end to end; `make seed` has to run first. IRR-78.

Coverage gaps are declared rather than padded: the pinned MLB results file holds full 2023-2025 and Apr-Jul 2015 only, with nothing for 2016-2022, so MLB backtests run over 2023-2025 and a missing-historical-periods quality check flags the gap on every build. NBA backtests use Oct-Dec slices only from the SBR archive, S-NHL-05 has no verified puck-line history and is forward-armed only, S-MLB-06 is forward-only by design, and multi-sport backtests cover only measured cross-sport overlap slates.

MODEL-grade payouts are estimates from assumed -110 or proxy lines and are labelled as such; backtests assume closing-line availability and ignore line movement, limits and fees; multi-sport legs assume independence with no correlation model and there are no same-game parlays in v1; Kalshi prices exclude exchange fees; and player and game props are not simulated at all because no free verified historical prop feed exists.

Twelve inherited NBA rows were 0-0 'finals' for games that had been postponed: nine are verified against published postponement notices and three are recorded as not played with verified=0 and an explicit 'reason NOT independently verified' note. Postponed games are never settled and never rated, and a ticket leg on one is voided with its stake refunded.

A flat-stake book can exceed its starting bankroll on paper, which the repository states rather than hides: equity curves, drawdowns and bankroll reconciliation are computed in economic time from ledger amounts, and the integrity checks fail the run on a negative balance, a drawdown above 100 percent or any drift against the recorded current amount.

value.description: Autonomous live book-maker lab for prediction markets, focused on pricing theory rather than profit: it builds a public-data-only order-book model for Kalshi contracts (books, candles, schedules, settlements, market metadata, series and fees) and models the three things a bookmaker must decide — the fair price, the price to quote and the price at which to stop quoting. The model assumes an order-flow process whose initial estimate of the fair value is wrong, models the informed side as having observed the outcome while the uninformed side is noisy, states a pure market-maker objective of capturing the spread, and prices an American binary option by valuing the asset at exercise and converting to an event probability through the inverse CDF — the midpoint between the bid and the ask is a price, not an expectation. It publishes a scoring guide for spread captures (a continuous book with depth at every price scores a capture, a depleted or one-sided book scores a price change, a stale book scores no capture), a venue-analysis guide framed as mid-price precision and a mirror-fill cost, a 61-category research log with the explicit caveat that a category is a hypothesis class rather than a conclusion, and a stated limit that thin books inflate Kelly fractions and that public-data candles are not always printable. data/candles/ holds 84 committed candle files (53 KXBTC, 31 KXETHD) from 12 series, including every contract month under the KXBTCD and KXETHD series with official fetch provenance, and data/manifest.json's series-catalog entry is a 17,505,797-byte full series catalog with volume, sha256 af04b45aabd739cd0d3f78d782b327cdb72e7c23e6300e45566319d2da28. The competition has not traded: data/season-2026/forward/leaderboard.json reports cycles_completed 0 with 10 strategies all still at $10,000.00, realized_pnl 0.0 and 0 fills, and data/season-2026/forward/{trades,intents,marks}.jsonl are each 0 lines. scripts/verify.py was executed here and reports passed 1198, errors 0 (its checks array lists 12 V1/V2 messages phrased as the failures they did not find, so the string 'missing provenance' in that output means the opposite), and `python3 -m pytest tests -q` reports 39 passed. A new data/season-2026/backtest/results.json records a candle-replay backtest that states its own assumptions in the artifact: signal on bar t close, fill at bar t+1 open with no look-ahead, candle-proxied touches that are explicitly NOT book-verified, a default 2-cent limit buffer capped at 0.99, cumulative-volume gates and signed slippage.

The verification gate passes but is only half exercised, and the way it reports is a trap for a reader. `check(ok, code, msg)` in scripts/verify.py appends msg to CHECKS when ok is True and to ERRORS when it is False, and every msg is phrased as the failure it did not find — so the printed `passed: 42` sits next to lines reading 'V1: hash mismatch exchange-status.json' and 'V13-trades: duplicate rows detected', which look like 42 failures and are 42 passes. `errors: 0` with exit code 0 is the authoritative signal. value.description: An autonomous, offline-first research engine: six numbered sources (arXiv, Crossref, GitHub, NIST NVD, PyPI, USGS), eleven named deterministic critic rules, nine published scoring criteria, a contradiction register that is never silently resolved, and a CLI that serves, publishes, re-verifies and reports. README.md at commit c492159 describes the pipeline as Compete (six personas build candidate answers made only of quotations plus fixed scaffolding), Criticise (eleven named rules attack each candidate, each attack recording the rule that fired) and Refuse when a source cannot be quoted. The generated run-a467fa87a6df site data (2026-09-23T00:55:17Z) reports 300 claims, 93 documents, 222 competing candidates carrying 960 recorded criticisms, 147 derived open questions, 12 contradictions awaiting a human decision, 102 discoveries, 4 topics, 5 experiments, 28 failures and 46 registered irregularities (23 info, 15 warning, 0 error) of which 38 are open and 8 resolved. Substance is measured rather than asserted: 42 of 300 claims are dated, 252 are quantified, the mean substance score is 0.5166 and 39.67 percent of the corpus is substantive rather than metadata. The run's own change scan attempted 6 sources and scanned 2: arXiv, Crossref, USGS and NVD all returned policy_refused because their robots.txt could not be fetched over the sandbox's TLS egress and RFC 9309 2.3.1.4 requires a crawler to assume complete disallow in that case, so no request was made to those hosts; GitHub and PyPI scanned and returned 13 new items between them. Its link checker reports 126 links checked, 106 ok and 20 failed, and records that the check ran on a GitHub Actions runner with unrestricted egress so that 'unreachable' is not mistaken for a broken link. Its own checks block additionally reports 159 claims without a link and 10 unsupported claims. The test suite was executed here: 189 passed.

It is now a 31-commit, 234-file application with its own engine package, test suite, evidence store and generated site. The placeholder description had become flatly false, which is the IRR-42 and IRR-64 failure class, and it is rewritten here from the repository's own files. IRR-84.

Three generated artifacts disagree about the size of the document store because a live engine wrote them at different moments: reports/site_data.json (23:12:31Z) counts 89 documents, reports/SUMMARY.md (23:22:59Z) says 91 retrieved documents stored and hashed and 5 experiments run rather than 3, and evidence/snapshots/ holds 94 files on disk at this commit. The machine-readable counts block is what this entry publishes, with its generation timestamp, and the divergence is recorded rather than reconciled.

The engine reports its own gaps instead of filling them: checks.claims_without_link is 159 of 300 claims, unsupported_claims is 10, unresolved_contradictions is 12 with 0 resolved, fixture_documents is 0, and at the time of this read sources_polled was 1 with sources_reached 0 and the CLI printed 'no recorded cycle found in reports/site_data.json; the sources table shows no reachability'. Verification thresholds are published and calibrated rather than implicit: a claim is supported at token coverage 0.8, partially supported at 0.45, with a verbatim quote minimum of 24.0 characters (state/calibration.json), and the calibration block records a baseline accuracy of 0.96 over 26 cases with its disagreements listed.

The root index.html is a one-page entry point that links into the generated site in docs/, which README.md states explicitly; Pages publishes from main / and a root index.html does exist there, so this entry classifies as app.

value.description: Bay Area vacation-planner and rain-risk evidence layer for a listener in San Francisco ZIP 94122, built only from committed verified national weather data (NOAA NCEI station USW00023272, GSOD 72494023234, ISD hourly 72494023234, plus NOAA Storm Events, which holds 119 San Francisco County records of which 99 are rain-related and whose damage column is recorded as unusable). The analysis window runs 2026-10-01 to 2027-01-31, a 123-day season with 6 cost drivers and 5 inputs, generated 2026-09-22T12:41:42Z. Across the 30-year seasonal summary the mean seasonal rainfall is 12.79 inches (median 13.26, range 1.71 to 22.82), the mean number of wet days at or above 0.01 inch is 34.5 (median 35.0, range 7.0 to 55.0 out of 123), and a run of 3 or more consecutive wet days occurs in 96.7% of the 30 seasons — 80.0% for a run of 5 or more, 53.3% for 7 or more, 23.3% for 10 or more, with the longest run averaging 7.3 days and reaching 17.0. Days at or above 0.25 inch average 14.97 and days at or above 1.00 inch average 3.19, against NOAA's published 14.9 and 3.26 — an agreement within 0.06 day. The season is classified El Niño: 11 of the 30 seasons on record were, and the probability of a 7-day-or-longer wet spell there is 81.8%. The repository refuses to publish a zero mean number of wet days per year; instead it shows a 29 x 13 matrix (each cell its own nonzero distribution) with a by-month table whose 12 means are 3.53, 3.24, 3.53, 2.77, 2.13, 1.37, 0.93, 0.83, 0.40, 0.27, 0.20 and 0.10, and the 0.2-inch and 1.0-inch stats produced from raw hourly totals where the derivation is reproducible in principle but not in practice from the site. The README records a concrete paper-trading action: at the 0.2-inch threshold and a 10.34% annual betting edge, $60 wagered 31 times against a 9-game accumulation window returned $271.80, a +$211.80 profit.

statement: MasterSite catalogs ShoulderPain — Research-Backed Shoulder & Scapula Pain Guide in Health & Personal Guides; its recorded Pages status is built.

value.description: Source-linked GitHub Pages guide to shoulder and shoulder-blade ('wing') pain, written around one stated context — a male adult aged about 36-40, left-side sleeping, a possible workout injury, prolonged computer use and limited room space — and explicitly educational information rather than a diagnosis or a personalised rehabilitation plan, with emergency and urgent warning signs given priority over exercises, furniture or symptom logging. Ten pages share one static template and compact navigation: start, medical advice, treatment, exercises, desk and room, furniture and prices, care costs, an optional log, sources and audit, and next steps; all research content works without JavaScript and no sign-in or symptom entry is required. The current revision is a deliberate narrowing rather than an expansion. It reviewed the pre-existing site at commit e1c63c4 and, in its own words, 'replaces blanket verification/completeness claims with a narrower, auditable source register, simplifies the UI and corrects unsafe or unverified assumptions', keeping the previous site in Git history. Twenty official pages were opened directly on 2026-09-20 — MedlinePlus, NHS, AAOS/ASES, CSP, OSHA, CMS, five furniture manufacturers or sellers, and Luna — and data/sources.json records each source's section, a short excerpt, its scope and its check date, with government and medical-society guidance kept separate from commercial product information. data/claims.json maps source-bearing content units to references and source-file lines: 90 review units, described as a review aid and 'not an automated truth certificate'. Exercises were reduced to four source-checked examples carrying exact AAOS HTML doses and supervision boundaries. Five furniture listings give exact variant and price boundaries with folding trade-offs, and no product is claimed to fit an unmeasured room or to treat shoulder pain; the one care price quoted is an official provider example ($135 self-pay per visit at Luna), not a nationwide average, and other unverified medical costs are explicitly left unpriced. REVIEW.md documents three passes and eight source irregularities found while reading, including a COMHOMA price where $54.49 was the selected White variant and $25.50 the discount, a VIVO desk that folds against the wall but is not quickly detached, a Lillipad whose specifications claim a 700 lb static test while its FAQ says 350 lb and neither replaces the 75 lb operational rating, and a Luna search excerpt showing $125 where both directly opened pages showed $135. The optional log is local-only, retains the `shoulderpain-log-v1` key so prior entries can still be read or imported if valid, and validates numbers, booleans, calendar dates and shape; invalid entries are counted and never rounded or silently converted, invalid persisted data blocks edits rather than being overwritten, raw JSON export is available for recovery, cross-tab changes block saves until reload, spreadsheet formula injection is mitigated on CSV export, and the bounded import size was raised to 20 MB so the 5,000-entry schema can import its own backups. Its former clinical 'improving/worsening' classifier and calendar-based advice were removed on the grounds that sparse logs should not reassure someone or postpone assessment, and the summary is now descriptive only. Validation reports 8 Node unit tests and 31 Chromium browser tests passing, automated axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 AA checks passing on all ten pages at 390px and 1440px, and no page-level horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768 or 1440px. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20.
flags: Its own verification policy refuses the strongest claims a directory reader might assume: 'Unknown or conflicting facts stay visibly unresolved. No claim of independent clinical verification or zero errors', and 'Automated checks cannot establish medical accuracy'. REVIEW.md adds that no clinician independently reviewed the personalised suitability of the information, and that link integrity, automated accessibility and browser tests are not medical validation.

Deliberately narrower than the version it replaced. The prior revision carried a 56-source register (S1-S56), four logged review passes, 32 logged corrections and a 32-row irregularity table; this one carries 20 opened sources, three passes, 8 source irregularities and a 6-row next-steps table. Its stated reason is worth quoting because it is the opposite of the usual instinct: 'The guide is a focused, source-linked starting set, not all possible diseases or products. Further expansion should improve evidence rather than inflate a count' (IRR-57).

Now has a build and test step, unlike the version previously described here: npm ci, npm run build (claim ledger plus ten static root HTML pages), npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser (Playwright) and npm run serve, with the shared page layout in tools/build.py and Python 3 and Node 22 used in validation. Visitors need neither. Committed root HTML means the Pages configuration needs no runtime build.

Browser tests were run against an npm-distributed Chromium 153 binary extracted outside Git because the standard Playwright browser download and Debian package retrieval were blocked by sandbox networking; REVIEW.md states plainly that 'this is not an unexecuted test claim', and CI uses the normal Playwright installation on GitHub-hosted runners. Remaining testing limits it names: no manual screen-reader-user audit, no cross-browser matrix, no third-party video-playback test, and automated accessibility is not full conformance certification.

Open limitations it lists for a next session: no clinician exam or clinical peer review and no systematic literature review; actual room fit, safe removal route and body/desk measurements unknown; no checked chair meets both the folding and the adjustable long-day-workstation criteria; product stock, prices and return policies change and Lillipad has contradictory page content; personal care and medicine costs, country and insurance remain unknown.

Changed state four times inside one audit and this description is the fourth rewrite — verified in sequence against 239eaa8 (01:25:47Z), dd1a7d4 (02:13:17Z), 6812ef3 (02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after a prior stamp had been written) and now 8a21b94 (03:07:51Z), which rebuilt all ten pages and reversed the sourcing method entirely (IRR-47, IRR-57).

Re-verified upstream on 21 September 2026: every medical, exercise and workstation source (M1-M6, E1-E3, W1-W3) was re-opened and all registered excerpts still match the official pages. Product rechecks succeeded only partially — VIVO and Lillipad were re-verified through official seller product-data endpoints, while fetch-proxy failures prevented re-opening IKEA, Branch, three manual/spec PDFs and the cost sources, whose entries stay dated 20 September 2026 and are labelled as such on the site. No price, stock or fit fact was invented for the items that could not be re-opened.
